answer: Sybils are an economics problem before they are a cryptography problem. With Proof of unique L2 sequencer fee payment record, fees paid on one rollup for two years becomes the price of admission, and the cipher is that the price is charged per identity. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that fees paid on one rollup for two years — so privacy survives, and the shale is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. Each clone pays the full price again — no bulk discount, no shared proof — and the ivory is exactly why the farm stays small or goes broke.
